title: Map At With Bounds Checking
description: Access map value with bounds checking (throws if key missing)
explanation: map::at() provides safe access that throws std::out_of_range if the key does not exist.

title: Map Contains C++20
description: Check if a key exists in a map (C++20)
explanation: contains() is a clearer alternative to count() or find() for checking key existence.

title: Map Try Emplace C++17
description: Try to insert a key-value pair without overwriting (C++17)
explanation: try_emplace constructs the value in-place only if the key is absent. Unlike emplace, it does not move from the key if insertion fails.

title: Map Insert Or Assign C++17
description: Insert or update a value efficiently (C++17)
explanation: insert_or_assign inserts if the key is absent or updates (assigns) if it exists. Returns an iterator and a bool.

title: Map Extract C++17
description: Extract a node from a map without copying (C++17)
explanation: Extracts a key-value pair as a node handle, allowing modification of the key and moving between maps without copying.

title: Map Merge C++17
explanation: Transfers all non-duplicate elements from one map to another without copying or moving.

title: Map Key Comparison Object
explanation: key_comp and value_comp return the comparison object used for ordering.
code:
auto cmp = mp.key_comp();
bool result = cmp(1, 2);  // true if 1 < 2

title: Map Emplace
description: Construct a key-value pair in-place in a map
explanation: emplace constructs the pair in-place, potentially avoiding a copy of the key or value.

title: Multimap Declaration
description: Declare a multimap allowing duplicate keys
explanation: multimap allows multiple key-value pairs with the same key. Does not support operator[] or at().

title: Map Reverse Traversal
description: Iterate over a map in reverse order
explanation: Use reverse iterators (rbegin/rend) to traverse the map in descending key order.

title: Map Erase By Iterator
description: Erase element from map using iterator (constant time amortized)
explanation: Erasing by iterator is amortized constant time, while erasing by key is O(log n).

title: Map Transparent Comparator C++14
description: Heterogeneous lookup in map using transparent comparator (C++14)
explanation: With a transparent comparator (std::less<>), find and lower_bound work with string_view literals without constructing a std::string.
